text:
mike: Heads-up: KV slab handoff appears to cause sustained residency growth for tenant 'alpha' when clients use long contexts (>32k). Profiling attached, reproduces locally with our longctx sim.

sarah: Oof. Any quick counters? evict_attempts vs page_walks?

mike: Quick snapshot from local run: pg_walks=12.4k, evict_attempts=8.9k, successful_evictions=1.2k, frag_ratio=0.72, reuse_miss_rate=0.31. The handoff path logs show a lot of "handoff-skip: owner_not_ready" spikes.

anita: If owner_not_ready is common we might be marking pages resident before the new slab owner has rebuilt its index, causing ghost entries that block proper reuse.

josh: I saw a similar pattern last month but with smaller longctx sizes — reuse_miss_rate spiked right after the handoff and never recovered for that tenant. Seems like the LRU window gets reset or poorly re-linked.

mike: Repro steps I ran: `./sim --multitenant 8 --longctx --handoff-interval 30s --trace-handshake` then filter logs for tenant alpha. Full trace: https://logs.internal/replay/175850/alpha-handoff-trace (internal).

ci-bot: build #3421 (eng-runtime/kv-handoff) completed in 6m :white_check_mark:

sarah: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) soft_quota that decays rather than immediate hard cap so a tenant can backfill without thrash, 2) handoff backoff if fragmentation > X and recent_reuse_rate < Y.

josh: Proposed heuristic: if fragment_ratio > 0.65 && reuse_miss_rate > 0.25 then postpone handoff by 200ms (gives owner time to re-link). Also try delaying mark-resident until post-compaction if compaction will reclaim contiguous slab.

anita: Add a compact-on-handoff pass only when fragmentation > 0.6 to avoid paying for compaction every time. The compaction cost is small vs repeated evict/rewarm cycles.

mike: Agree. I'll prototype a "handoff-smoothing" mode. Metrics to add: tenant_kv_handoff_latency, tenant_kv_fragmentation_pct, tenant_kv_reuse_miss_rate.

sarah: Can you attach the exact config you used for the sim? makes it easier to reproduce on CI harness.

mike: Here's the minimal config snippet I ran locally: \n```\nevict_policy: SMOOTH_QUOTA\nsoft_quota_pct: 0.85\nbackoff_ms: 200\ncompaction_threshold: 0.6\nhandoff_mark_delay_ms: 50\n```\n
josh: Nice. Can we also gate the handoff frequency behind a token bucket so a noisy tenant can't trigger repeated handoffs every second?

anita: Yes — token bucket or exponential backoff both work. Token bucket is easier to reason about with quotas.

mike: I'll add both options to the sim and run a comparative sweep. Will create a tiny repro script for oncall to exercise: `scripts/kv-handoff-repro.sh --tenant alpha --burst 100`.

sarah: Ping @infra and @platform-run to spin up a 4x larger testbed once you have the PR; we should validate at scale.

mike: Will do, opening PR today with experiment dashboard + perf counters. ETA ~48h for initial PR, 2 weeks for full dashboard and CI job.

anita: Recommend we land only metric exports + a feature-flagged smoothing patch first, then iterate on compaction/backoff tuning. Less blast radius.

mike: Sounds good. I'll add a feature flag `kv.handoff_smoothing.enabled` default false and a rollout plan (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).

josh: For the canary, also emit per-tenant alerts when fragmentation delta > 0.2 in 5m window so we catch regressions.

mike: Will add alert rule and dashboard panels. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sarah: Assign to eng-runtime sprint next cycle? owner: mike, reviewers: anita, josh.

mike: Yep — assigned and PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/4212

josh: Great — post PR link in this thread so oncall can find it quick.

mike: Done. I'll follow up with sim results tomorrow morning.
